sub_units.name: What is HTML?
sub_units.content: Array traversal refers to visiting each element of an array one by one to perform operations such as reading, updating, or computing values. Basic operations on arrays include insertion, deletion, updating elements, and calculating values like sum, minimum, and maximum. Understanding traversal and these fundamental operations is essential for solving many programming problems efficiently.

sub_units.name: Setting Up Environment
sub_units.content: Searching in arrays involves finding the position of a specific element. The most basic method is linear search, which checks each element sequentially. For sorted arrays, binary search can be used to reduce search time significantly by repeatedly dividing the search space in half. Understanding these searching techniques helps improve algorithm efficiency.

sub_units.name: HTML Document Structure
sub_units.content: Array rearrangement problems involve changing the order of elements based on specific conditions. Examples include moving all zeros to the end, separating positive and negative numbers, alternating elements, or sorting based on certain criteria. These problems help develop strong skills in in-place algorithms and efficient array manipulation.

sub_units.name: First Web Page
sub_units.content: Subarray problems focus on contiguous segments of an array. Many algorithmic challenges involve finding subarrays with maximum or minimum sums, specific conditions, or certain lengths. Techniques like prefix sums and Kadane’s algorithm are commonly used to efficiently solve these problems.
